artworks.title: Heracles Strangling the Serpents
artworks.description: Louvre stamnos: the infant in the cradle throttles Hera's snakes while Iphicles recoils — the Theban birth that proves Zeus' son.

artworks.title: Boy Heracles Strangling a Snake
artworks.description: Capitoline marble: the chubby child grips a writhing serpent — the cradle miracle sculpted as innate heroic strength.

artworks.title: The Choice of Hercules
artworks.description: Carracci's young hero at the crossroads of Virtue and Pleasure — the arduous path that follows the cradle and precedes Eurystheus' labours.

artworks.title: Farnese Hercules
artworks.artist: After Lysippos (signed by Glykon of Athens)
artworks.description: The exhausted strongman after the labours — the end-state of the child who strangled serpents and was banished into Eurystheus' service.

films.title: Hercules
films.description: Disney's cradle snakes and banishment-to-mortality rewrite the Theban birth — baby Heracles strangling Hera's serpents for a family audience.

music.title: Hercules
music.description: Handel's oratorio-drama turns on the hero's domestic catastrophe — madness, Megara's shadow, and the cost of strength after the labours' fame.

popCulture.title: Herakles (Euripides)
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides stages the madness that slays Megara's children — the Theban homecoming that turns the infant serpent-strangler into a polluted exile.

popCulture.title: Heracles
popCulture.description: From Alcmene's cradle to Eurystheus' service — the birth, the serpents, and the Delphic banishment that open the labours.
